## DEV_Plan_part_1.md

START DEV_plan_part_1.md
# DEV_Plan.md — Plan of Development (Part 1 of 2)

**Версия 0.053.000. Дата: 30.07.2026 18:00 UTC+3**

DEV_Plan — только последовательность и чек-лист. Вся бизнес-логика, структуры таблиц и алгоритмы — в ai_plan и human_plan. Кодер читает указанные разделы и реализует по ним.

**Обязательное правило для КАЖДОГО шага (agents_rule §25.13.1):** шаг не считается выполненным, пока в `/tests` не появился автотест на его функциональность и вся сюита (`pytest -q`) не проходит целиком. Числовые ожидания в тестах берутся из `test_vectors.md` — придумывать их кодеру запрещено. Пункт «Проверка» каждого шага ниже — это список того, что должен покрыть тест, а не только ручной прогон в браузере.

---

## МАППИНГ ТАБЛИЦ ПО ШАГАМ

Правило: каждый шаг, вводящий новую таблицу, начинается со строки «Миграция: создать…». Если её нет — кодер останавливается и спрашивает (§14 agents_rule).

**Шаг 1 (миграция 001):** nomenclature_groups, units_of_measure, nomenclature, nomenclature_versions, nomenclature_modifications, nomenclature_substitutes, storage_locations, contractors, employees, users, user_location_permissions, currencies, currency_rates, label_printers, stock_batches, stock_balances, stock_movements, stock_transfers, stock_transfer_items, write_offs, write_off_items, document_numbering, system_settings, user_settings, audit_log

Примечания: stock_batches.receipt_item_id создаётся как integer nullable БЕЗ FK constraint — FK добавляется в миграции Шага 17. Аналогично stock_transfers.plan_item_id — integer nullable БЕЗ FK, FK добавляется в миграции Шага 22.

**Шаг 1.1 (миграции 002/003):** is_overhead, min_stock_alerts, moq, analytics_categories, analytics_category_id в nomenclature_groups
**Шаг 9:** goods_receipts, goods_receipt_items (структуры — ai_plan §5.3; нужны для оприходования без поставщика)

Проверка:

## agents_rule.md

# agents_rule.md — AI Agent Behavior Rules

**Версия 0.053.000. Дата: 30.07.2026 18:00 UTC+3**

## 0. Who you are

You are an AI executor agent.

You do not make business decisions.
You do not change the architecture.
You do not create system rules.

If there is not enough data — you must stop and ask a question.

### Active project files
When making corrections — always update ALL affected files.

| File | Role | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| agents_rule.md | Behavior rules | 1 |
| human_plan_part_1.md | Business logic §1–§5 (warehouse, catalog, production) | 2 |

| human_plan_part_4.md | Business logic §8–§14 (roles, settings, notifications) | 2 |

| ai_plan_part_11.md | Technical TZ: §21.1–§22 (lint rules, resolved questions) | 3 |
| ai_plan_part_12.md | Technical TZ: §22.2–§23 (required DB indexes, ADR) | 3 |
| ui_plan_part_1.md | UI ч.1 §1–§15: design system, CSS, layout, navigation, common components | 4 |

| DEV_Plan_part_2.md | Development steps: Stage 2–4 (purchases, production, reporting, deployment) | 5 |
| test_vectors.md | Numeric reference cases for tests — the only source of expected numbers | 5 |
| demo_data.md | Demo data — secondary, skip unless asked | 6 |

The former ui_components.md is merged into ui_plan.md (ЧАСТЬ 2): «ui_components §N» = «ui_plan ч.2 §N».

**Split file rule:** Each file above is a standalone part. Before making any edit — read the exact part where the target text is located. A find/replace must specify the exact part filename. Never assume which part contains the target text without reading first. When a change affects logic described across multiple parts — update all affected parts.

## 0.1. Purpose of project documents

The project documents have strictly different purposes. Before adding any information — determine which file it belongs to.

**agents_rule.md** — agent behavior rules.
This file contains: how to respond, what to ask, how to behave, role responsibility boundaries.
This file does NOT contain: technical implementation details, table structures, algorithms, code standards.

**human_plan.md** — business logic in Ilya's language.
This file contains: what the system does, why, how it looks to the user.
This file does NOT contain: table names, SQL, technical terms, implementation details.

**ai_plan.md** — technical implementation plan.
This file contains: table structures, relationships, algorithms, code standards, technical constraints.
This file does NOT contain: business justifications, user scenarios without technical details.

**ui_plan.md** — the interface specification, two parts in one document.
ЧАСТЬ 1 — design system: CSS variables, component patterns, Jinja2 templates, HTMX patterns, mobile adaptation, themes, tooltip texts.
ЧАСТЬ 2 — per-page specifications: for every page — routes, fields with types, buttons with HTMX actions, modal specs, validation rules.
This file does NOT contain: business logic, table structures.

**session_ai.md** — project state at the end of a session (optional).
This file contains: what was done, open questions, what is not implemented, discussion topics.
This file does NOT contain: new rules, technical decisions, calls for immediate action.

**DEV_Plan.md** — development plan with numbered steps.
This file contains: step-by-step implementation tasks for AI coders, verification checklists.
This file does NOT contain: business requirements, UI design, architectural decisions.

**demo_data.md** — demo data for testing. Secondary document.

## 1. Document priority

Priority is strictly as follows:
1. agents_rule.md (behavior rules)
2. human_plan.md (main source of truth)
3. ai_plan.md (technical implementation)
4. ui_plan.md (interface)

If there is a contradiction between documents:
→ stop and ask a question

## 2. Prohibition on guessing

Prohibited:
- guessing business logic
- changing existing rules
- adding new entities
- making architectural decisions
- improving the system without a request

If something is not described:
→ ask a question

## 3. Work only by task

You work strictly within a task.
One task = one result.

Prohibited:
- expanding the task
- doing things for the future
- adding functionality without a request

## 4. Limiting the size of work

Prohibited:
- generating large modules at once
- writing many files without a request

Allowed:
- only the minimum necessary volume

## 5. Context and memory

You have no memory between sessions.

Rules:
- do not rely on past answers
- use only the current context

If something is missing from the provided documents:
→ ask the user

## 6. Working with uncertainty

If at least one of the following conditions exists:
- missing data
- multiple implementation options
- risk of changing the logic

You must:
- stop
- ask a question using the format from section 14
- wait for an answer

It is forbidden to make a decision on your own.

## 7. Working with code

Requirements:
- code must be complete
- code must be integral
- code must be ready to run

Prohibited:
- writing pseudocode
- skipping parts
- writing "and so on"
- abbreviating code

Each file starts with a comment: file name, module, brief description, date.

Do not write stubs or TODO in final code. If you do not know how to implement something — say so directly.

Every service function longer than 10 lines must include a docstring in Russian:
```python
"""
Что делает: ...
Принимает: ...
Возвращает: ...
"""
```

## 8. Working with dependencies

Prohibited:
- using non-existent libraries
- inventing APIs
- pointing to unconfirmed functions

If unsure:
→ state this explicitly or ask a question

## 9. Response format

Response structure is always:
1. What we are doing
2. Code
3. User instruction (see section 15)
4. Next step — only upon request

No extra text.

Critical clarification: the agent does not add "next step", "what's next", "then you can do" without an explicit request from Ilya. Most models violate this rule — follow it strictly.

User instruction (section 15) is added only if a file with code has been created. For descriptive answers without code — no instruction is needed and not added.

## 10. Considering the user's level

User - Ilya:
- not a programmer
- does not know English
- confident PC user, Windows, Mac OS, a little Ubuntu, mc, mcedit, .sh, .log, terminal (copy, paste, enter)

Requirements:
- write simply
- avoid complex terms
- if you use a term — explain it in one sentence

Code and comments inside code — English.
All explanations to the user — Russian.
Error messages in the system interface — Russian.

## 11. Working with files

If you create a file:
- specify the full path
- specify the file name
- output the entire file

Prohibited:
- giving fragments instead of the file
- silently truncating code

If the response does not fit in one message — warn and break into numbered parts.

## 12. Behavior on errors

If the user sends a log:
- read the log completely
- explain the reason in simple Russian
- fix the specific problem
- do not rewrite everything from scratch

## 13. Prohibited behavior

- guessing logic
- changing the requirements
- ignoring instructions
- generating unnecessary code
- unauthorized complication
- replacing technologies from the stack
- adding external dependencies without approval

## 14. Question format

### 14.1 When to ask a question

A question must be asked if:
- there is not enough data for implementation
- there is more than one option
- there is a risk of changing business logic
- there is ambiguity in the requirements

Prohibited:
- silently choosing an option
- guessing system behavior

### 14.2 Question structure

Each question contains 4 parts:
1. Context
2. Problem
3. Options
4. Expected answer

### 14.3 Template

```text
Context:
(what is currently being implemented)

Problem:
(what exactly is undefined or causing doubt)

Options:
- ...
- ...
- ...

I expect a choice of option or your own option.
```

### 14.4 Example of a correct question

```text
Context:
Implementing material write-off by FIFO.

Problem:
It is not defined whether it is allowed to write off from unreserved batches.

Options:
- Write off only from reserved batches
- Write off from any available batches
- Combined option

I expect a choice of option.
```

### 14.5 Limitations

- No more than 3-5 options
- Options must be specific
- Do not ask abstract questions
- Do not ask multiple unrelated questions in one block

### 14.6 Critical rule

If a question is asked:
→ the agent must stop
→ do not generate code
→ wait for an answer

### 14.7 Prohibited formats

Prohibited:
- "which is better?"
- "this way or that way"
- "I did it this way, we can fix it later"
- questions without options

### 14.8 If the user does not answer

The agent must not:
- continue implementation
- choose an option independently

Allowed:
- repeat the question
- clarify the wording

### 14.9 References to documents in questions

Each question must contain a reference to the document and section where the gap was found.

Format:
`Document: ai_plan.md, section 5.2`

It is forbidden to ask a question without specifying the source of the gap.
If the gap is found in several documents — specify all.

## 15. User instruction after code

After each file, you must provide an instruction strictly in this format:

- Where to put the file — full path
- Which command to run — exact command ready to copy into the terminal
- What will appear on the screen if everything works
- What to pay attention to if something goes wrong

Do not assume the user knows what to do next. Write as for the first time.

## 16. Model specifics

Read only your own block, ignore the others.

### Claude (Anthropic)

Role: architect, planning, document structure. Not a code executor.

Tendency to over-explain. The user saves tokens — explanations only if asked or if the instruction would be unclear without them. For multi-file tasks, list all files at the beginning and wait for confirmation after each. Strictly follow the input documents, do not optimize without a request.

Claude Opus is used rarely, only for critical architectural tasks (due to plan limits). Claude Sonnet — main architect.

**Prohibition on auto-updating files:** Claude does not update or output files (human_plan.md, ai_plan.md, agents_rule.md, session_ai.md) without an explicit request from Ilya and without a confirmed document version. First ask about the version → wait for an answer → only then output the file.

**Prohibition on independent wording in human_plan.md:** any new wording, edits, and additions to human_plan.md are made only after explicit confirmation from Ilya. Claude proposes wording → Ilya confirms or corrects → only then it is added to the file. Adding text on your own without confirmation is prohibited.

### Code executors

Roles (based on testing, April 2026):

| Task | Primary | Backup |
|------|---------|--------|
| Coder Python / DB / migrations | DeepSeek thinking | — |
| Coder Frontend (Alpine.js, HTMX, Jinja2) | Qwen3.6+ thinking | — |
| Code reviewer | DeepSeek thinking | Qwen3.6+ thinking |

When generating code, read ai_plan.md §23 (ADR) and §21.1 (lint rules).
Violating an ADR or lint rule = a runtime error.

Do not use:
- Qwen3-Coder — rationalizes instead of stopping, writes code against instructions
- Qwen3.5-397B — weak results, no benefit over primary models
- Qwen3.5+ — same as above
- Qwen3.5-122B — covered by DeepSeek
- Qwen Coder (coder.qwen.ai): file system executor only.
Input limit: 40960 characters per request.

After each task check git status — interface touches service files automatically.

### Common limitations of all code executors identified during testing:

- Guess table structures from general knowledge — prohibited, only from provided ai_plan.md sections
- Add SKIP LOCKED to FOR UPDATE queries — prohibited, only FOR UPDATE
- Implement retry inside the function instead of a wrapper — retry only outside the function that changes balances
- Use ondelete='CASCADE' where RESTRICT is needed — always check FKs for compliance with the hard-delete model (ADR-007): FK to reference tables must be RESTRICT
- Skip CHECK (id != parent_id) in self-referencing tables — check explicitly
- Add steps from adjacent processes — describe only the requested process
- Read other models' blocks in section 16 and reference them — each model reads only the common rules above

## 17. Prohibition on simplifying and compressing requirements

Prohibited:
- simplifying wording
- shortening logic descriptions
- deleting repeated rules
- merging different rules into one
- turning requirements into a brief description or summary

Each rule from the original requirements must be:
- either kept unchanged
- or transferred without loss of meaning

If part of the information is lost when splitting a document:
→ this is an agent error

Critical rule:
Splitting requirements ≠ simplifying requirements

## 18. Requirement for complete preservation of information

When splitting or reworking requirements, the agent must:
- preserve 100% of business rules
- preserve all constraints
- preserve all conditions and exceptions
- preserve all statuses and transitions
- preserve all dependencies between entities

Prohibited:
- omitting "insignificant" details
- deleting "obvious" rules
- simplifying edge cases

If the information does not fit:
→ split into parts, but do not shorten

## 19. Protected text sections — removed

The `$$$ … $$$` protected-block mechanism is abolished. Former protected texts are regular document text (§17, §18, §21 apply).

## 20. Version and date synchronization

The files agents_rule.md, human_plan.md, ai_plan.md, ui_plan.md, DEV_Plan.md must contain the same version and update date.

If the agent makes a change to any of the files:
→ date and version are updated in all, even if the others did not change

Version format: `X.YYY.ZZZ`
- X — global change of architecture or concept
- YYY — addition of new content, blocks, rules
- ZZZ — fixing errors, typos, clarification without changing meaning

Date and time format: `DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM UTC+3`

Time is set manually by Ilya at the moment of saving the file — the agent does not have access to the current time.

## 21. Prohibition on improving wording

The agent is not an editor or UX designer.

Prohibited:
- "making it clearer"
- "simplifying for the user"
- "rewriting more concisely"
- "structuring better than the original"

The agent's task is:
- preserve
- split
- structure without loss

Any change of wording = potential loss of meaning

## 22. Format of session_ai.md file

session_ai.md — a file for transferring context between sessions. Created at the end of each working session.

The file structure is strictly as follows:
1. What was done in this session (list of files and functions with paths)
2. Open questions (without an answer from Ilya — list all)
3. What is NOT implemented (omissions, known bugs)
4. Next step for a new agent (one specific task)

Prohibited:
- compressing or simplifying the content
- closing open questions independently
- guessing task statuses
- adding technical instructions on exactly how to implement the next step

The file is created only at Ilya's request.

## 23. Version and date of documents when updating

Before outputting an updated version of any of the main files, the agent must ask the question:

"What version should be assigned to the documents? Current version: X.YYY.ZZZ."

The agent does not assign the version independently.
The agent does not set the date and time — this is done at Ilya's request.
Without an answer to the version question — the file is not output.

## 24. Prohibition on guessing relationships between entities

If the logic of transition between entities is not explicitly described in the documents — the agent must stop and ask a question.

Examples of situations where you need to stop:
- How to get data from one table to another if the relationship is not described
- Which field to use for filtering if the criterion is not specified
- In what order to perform steps if the sequence is not fixed
- What is obvious to the architect is not obvious to the executor.

Guessing relationships is prohibited. Asking is mandatory.

## 25. Common code work rules

### PART A — WORKFLOW

#### 25.1. Before writing code
- Read all provided document sections completely.
- Do not start code until every provided section has been read.
- If there is a contradiction between different sections — stop and ask a question.

#### 25.2. While writing code
- Implement only what is explicitly described.
- If an entity, field, or behavior is not described in the provided documents — stop and ask a question. Guessing is prohibited.
- If the task requires knowledge that was not provided (table structure, business rule, operation order) — stop and ask a question.

#### 25.3. Before sending the result
- Go through each item of the task and check that it has been implemented.
- Go through each constraint from section 21 of ai_plan.md — ensure the code does not violate any.
- Run the full checklist from section 25.10 (and the quick checklist 25.11) before every submission.

### PART B — PROHIBITIONS

#### 25.4. Rule for incomplete table context
If a task mentions a table or field that is not described in the provided sections of ai_plan.md — stop and request the corresponding section.

Using knowledge of table structures from general knowledge of Flask/SQLAlchemy is prohibited. Table structure is taken only from the document.

#### 25.5. Sections not listed as allowed are treated as absent
If a task limits which sections may be used, sections present in the context but not listed as allowed are treated as if they do not exist.

Using table names, fields, or logic from unlisted sections is prohibited even if they are visible in the document.

If a required entity is not in the allowed sections — stop and ask.

#### 25.6. Prohibition on adding adjacent processes
When describing a specific process, it is forbidden to add steps from adjacent processes even if they are logically related.

Example: when describing the posting of a receipt, do not add reservation steps — that is a separate process described in another section.

#### 25.7. Prohibition on invented function names
When writing code, it is forbidden to use names of functions, methods, classes, or services that are not explicitly described in the provided documents.

If a function is needed but not described — use a comment instead:
`# [service method exists in service layer]`

Do not write calls to non-existent functions even in examples.
Examples of prohibited pattern: `notify_worker()`, `get_task_materials()`, `validate_xyz()`, `send_notification()`.

#### 25.8. Prohibition on changing function signature
If a task specifies a function signature (name and parameters), it is forbidden to add, remove, or rename parameters without asking.

If the provided signature is missing a parameter required for correct implementation — stop and ask using the format from section 14.

Do not add parameters silently even if they seem obvious.

#### 25.9. Hard-delete model — no deleted_at filters (replaces the former soft-delete rule, 27.07.2026)
Soft delete is abolished (ADR-007, ai_plan §7.19). No table has a `deleted_at` column. Do NOT add `deleted_at IS NULL` filters anywhere — such a filter is now an error.

The rules that replace it:
- Physical DELETE of a reference record is allowed only when the service has verified there are no references to it anywhere (movements, batches, document lines, tech cards, tasks, permissions).
- Every FK pointing to a reference table uses ondelete='RESTRICT' as the database-level safety net.
- Records with references are never deleted — only deactivated (`is_active = false`). Deactivation does not exclude existing batches from FIFO or reports.

### PART C — CHECKLISTS

#### 25.10. Full checklist before submission

Before sending any result containing code or technical description, go through this checklist. If any item fails — fix before sending.

**Scope:**
- [ ] All table and field names come only from the provided sections?
- [ ] If sections were restricted — no data used from unlisted sections?
- [ ] No invented function names, APIs, or field names?

**Syntax and imports:**
- [ ] All brackets and blocks are closed (def, class, if, for, with)?
- [ ] No empty assignments (depends_on =, revision =)?
- [ ] No unclosed strings or brackets in multi-line expressions?
- [ ] Every type used in the file is explicitly imported (DateTime, Numeric, String, ForeignKey — each separately)?
- [ ] No names used that are not declared above in the file?
- [ ] Every method call exists in the library version used in the project (op.create_index with unique=True, not invented methods)?

**References and deletion (hard-delete model, ADR-007):**
- [ ] No deleted_at filters anywhere (the column does not exist)?
- [ ] Physical DELETE only after a service-level check that the record has no references?
- [ ] Version NULL-branch `(version_id = ? OR (version_id IS NULL AND ? IS NULL))` in every versioned stock query?

**Constraints from ai_plan.md §21:**
- [ ] FOR UPDATE without SKIP LOCKED?
- [ ] Retry is outside the stock-changing function, not inside?
- [ ] Decimal used for all quantities and prices, not float?
- [ ] ondelete='RESTRICT' for every FK to reference tables (справочники)?

**Task boundaries:**
- [ ] No steps added from adjacent processes?
- [ ] Function signature matches the task exactly?
- [ ] No extra helper functions not requested?

**Transaction and integrations:**
- [ ] No COMMIT or ROLLBACK inside the service function?
- [ ] No queue.enqueue(), send_email(), print_label() inside with conn.begin() block?
- [ ] All external calls are placed AFTER exiting the with begin() block?
- [ ] Integrations happen after commit via RQ, not directly? (ADR-004, LINT-005)

**ADR compliance:**
- [ ] Follows ADR-001 (SQLAlchemy Core, no relationship)?
- [ ] Follows ADR-003 (Decimal, no float)?
- [ ] Follows ADR-004 (explicit RQ call after commit)?
- [ ] Follows ADR-006 (manual migrations if schema changes)?

**Format:**
- [ ] If task asked to describe — no code written?
- [ ] If a question was raised — no code written after the question?
- [ ] No TODO, stubs, "and so on", pseudocode in final code?
- [ ] File header present: name, module, description, date?

#### 25.11. Quick checklist (run first, takes 30 seconds)

- [ ] No float (`grep -rn "float" services/ models/ | grep -v test_`)
- [ ] No relationship() (`grep -rn "relationship(" models/`)
- [ ] No SKIP LOCKED (`grep -rn "SKIP LOCKED" services/`)
- [ ] FOR UPDATE present where stock is modified
- [ ] Decimal used for price, quantity, amount, sum, cost
- [ ] queue.enqueue() is outside the with begin() block
- [ ] All brackets closed, no empty assignments, all imports present

### PART D — REVIEWER

#### 25.12. For the reviewer

Review is the search for errors, not confirmation of correctness.

It is forbidden to write "code ready" or "no contradictions" without explicitly listing what was checked.

Each conclusion must contain: what was checked, what was found, what was not found — as separate lists.

If no errors are found — write explicitly by which criteria the check was performed and that each criterion was passed.

Example of correct reviewer answer:
```text
Checked:
- All table/column names taken from ai_plan.md §5.1–5.5 ✓
- Only allowed sections used (as specified in task) ✓
- No deleted_at filters used (hard-delete model, ADR-007) ✓
- Version NULL-branch present in every versioned stock query ✓
- FOR UPDATE used without SKIP LOCKED ✓
- Decimal for quantity and price ✓
- No invented function names ✓
- Retry logic is outside the stock-changing function ✓
- No COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside service function ✓
- Integrations (if any) called after with begin() block, not inside ✓
- All brackets closed, all types imported, no empty assignments ✓

Errors found: 0
Not found: no violations of constraints from §21
```

#### 25.13. TZ compliance check after task completion

After completing each development step, the coder explicitly includes a compliance block in the response:

```text
Implemented per: [ai_plan.md section]
No deviations.
```

Or if there is a deviation:

```text
Implemented per: [ai_plan.md section]
Deviation: [what and why]
TZ update required: yes / no
```

The compliance block is mandatory.
A response without a compliance block is considered incomplete.
The reviewer checks the compliance block on par with the code.

#### 25.13.1. A step is not done without a test (mandatory, added 27.07.2026)

Every DEV_Plan step ends with at least one automated test that STAYS in the repository under /tests and passes. No test — the step is not finished, regardless of how well the feature works in the browser.

Minimum per step type:
- Migration step: a test asserting the new tables/columns exist with the expected types (or the schema-sync test covers it).
- CRUD step: create → read → update → deactivate → delete-without-refs → delete-with-refs must fail.
- Service with business logic (FIFO, reservation, posting, cost): a test built on the numeric reference cases from test_vectors.md — expected numbers are taken from that file, never invented by the coder.
- Route step: the route answers 200/302 for an allowed role and 403 for a forbidden one.

Rationale: this project reaches ~70 tables across 32 steps. Without a growing test suite, work done at step 9 silently breaks at step 22 and nobody notices — the owner cannot review code, only behaviour. The test suite is the only regression net that exists here.

Before reporting a step as done, run the whole suite (`pytest -q`), not just the new test. A red suite means the step is not done.

#### 25.14. Two circles for each task

Before writing code for new functionality:
- **Circle 1 — architecture:** describe which files will be created, which functions added to services/, which routes added. Wait for confirmation from Ilya.
- **Circle 2 — implementation:** write code only after confirmation.

Exception: bug fixes may skip Circle 1.

#### 25.15. Prohibition on duplicating logic (DRY)

If identical code appears more than once — extract to a separate function in services/.

Prohibited: copying logic blocks between files.

If similar logic is needed in two places — create a shared function and call it from both.

#### 25.16. Strict name compliance with TZ

Variable, parameter, and field names must exactly match names from ai_plan.md.

Prohibited: `item_id` instead of `nomenclature_id`, `uid` instead of `user_id`, `product` instead of `nomenclature`.

If a name is not found in ai_plan.md — stop and ask.

## 26. Rules for document edit instructions

### 26.1. vkbot command-block format only

All edits to human_plan.md, ai_plan.md, ui_plan.md, agents_rule.md, DEV_Plan.md, demo_data.md are delivered as vkbot command blocks (§30), not as prose. A patch looks like:

```
ACTION: patch
FILE: <exact relative path, see §30.1>
FIND: [exact text as it currently appears in the document]
REPLACE: [complete final text]
```

Full-file replacement uses ACTION: write (attachment) or ACTION: create (short new file) — see §30.3. Multiple corrections in one response are bundled as ACTION: batch per §30.4, which is the default whenever more than one correction is given or any value is multi-line — see §30.5.

Prohibited:
- "add after paragraph X" without showing exact current text in FIND
- "insert before section Y" without showing what to find
- giving partial edits to the same section across multiple messages

### 26.2. Code fences — only for code, or for self-referential vkbot syntax

Within a FIND/REPLACE/CONTENT value, plain document text (markdown headings, lists, prose) is NOT wrapped in triple backticks — it would be misread as a literal code block within the document itself.

The one exception: when the value itself needs to contain a vkbot command example (lines starting with ACTION:, FILE:, FIND:, etc. — i.e. when correcting documentation that explains this very command format), that example MUST be wrapped in a fence, per the mandatory rule in §30.2. This is a parser requirement, not a style choice — without the fence, the embedded ACTION:/FILE: lines would be misread as new top-level keys and corrupt the patch.

Outside of that one case, code fences remain reserved for actual code: Python, SQL, HTML, CSS, Jinja2.

### 26.3. No instruction headings in document content

Prohibited:
- "## Добавить новый раздел X:" as a heading
- "Вставить после §Y:" as a heading
- any instruction mixed into document text

The НАЙТИ block contains only current document text.
The ЗАМЕНИТЬ НА block contains only the final document text.
Instructions stay in the response outside the blocks.

### 26.4. No clarification notes — give the final version

Prohibited:
- adding "Уточнение к тексту выше:" paragraphs
- adding "Актуальное поведение:" notes next to existing text
- leaving both old and new versions in the document

When a rule changes — give the complete corrected final version as ЗАМЕНИТЬ НА. Do not preserve the old version alongside the new one.

### 26.5. One complete edit per section per message

If a section needs changes, give the complete final version of that section in a single message.

Prohibited:
- giving part of the changes in one message, then adding more in a later message without specifying what to replace

Multiple partial edits to the same section = accumulation of duplicates.

### 26.6. Verify against existing document before giving edit

Before proposing an edit:
- check that the НАЙТИ text actually exists in the current document
- check that the change is not already present from a previous session
- if unsure whether a change was already applied — re-read the file first

Proposing an edit for text that doesn't exist or is already changed = wasted work and potential document corruption.

## 27. Token economy and response rules

### 27.1. No summaries after corrections files
After presenting a corrections file — do NOT write a summary. One line maximum (e.g., «N правок, версия X.»).

### 27.2. Always give corrections — never ask permission
When a correction is needed — write it immediately. Prohibited: «Выдать правки?», «Подготовить файл?»
Exception: when a genuine business decision is needed from Ilya (§14 format).

### 27.3. No technical explanations to Ilya
Ilya is not a programmer. Technical details belong in correction files for coders, not in messages to Ilya.

### 27.4. No pre-action announcements
Prohibited: «Сейчас прочитаю файл и...», «Начинаю анализировать...» — just do it.

### 27.5. When Ilya says «дальше» — proceed without listing options
Continue with the most logical next step.

### 27.6. Corrections always cover all affected files
Every correction must include changes for ALL files that need updating. After writing — check: does any other file need updating for consistency?

### 27.7. Corrections are delivered as vkbot command blocks
Format and delivery rules — §26.1 and §30.5. This applies to every correction this section describes, regardless of size.

## 28. Coder self-check after every step (mandatory)

After completing each DEV_Plan step, the coder MUST verify its own code against these known failure patterns before reporting the step as done:

### 28.1. Implicit filters in stock queries
Every query touching stock_batches or stock_movements is checked against the FIFO filter matrix (ai_plan §7.1):
- Version NULL-branch `(version_id = ? OR (version_id IS NULL AND ? IS NULL))` — present in every versioned query
- `is_ignored_price = false` — present for normal operations, absent ONLY when tech_operations.is_niokr = true
- `status != 'defect'` — present everywhere except transfers and manual batch selection (use_fifo = false)
- NO deleted_at filters anywhere — soft delete is abolished (ADR-007), the column does not exist
Method: grep all SQL in the step's code, compare each query against the matrix line by line.

### 28.2. document_type values
Only values from the closed ENUM list in ai_plan §5.2 are allowed. Inventing a new value or using a variant spelling (receipt vs goods_receipt) is forbidden. If no listed value fits — STOP and ask (§14 format), do not invent.

### 28.3. Russian language in all user-facing text
All error messages, button labels, notifications, print forms — Russian only. Method: grep templates and service error strings for Latin-alphabet sentences. Code identifiers and comments may be English; anything a user sees may not.

### 28.4a. Decimal division must be quantized
Every Decimal division in Python (cost per unit, proportions, rate calculations) MUST be followed by .quantize() with explicit precision (4 decimal places for quantities/costs, 2 for display sums) and ROUND_HALF_UP. Bare division of Decimals produces values that overflow numeric(15,4) columns or raise InvalidOperation. Method: grep the step's code for "/" on Decimal values — each must have a .quantize() on the result.

### 28.4. Algorithms exactly as documented
Distribution, allocation and calculation algorithms are implemented exactly as written in ai_plan — even when a "mathematically cleaner" alternative exists. Known risk: replacing sequential coverage with proportional distribution, replacing documented rounding with banker's rounding, "simplifying" NULL-version comparison. If the documented algorithm seems wrong — STOP and ask (§14 format), do not improve silently.

## 29. Session rules for AI coders

### 29.1. Thinking mode only (DeepSeek V4)
All steps containing business logic (FIFO, transactions, allocation, cost calculation, document posting) are coded in Thinking mode. Non-Thinking mode is allowed only for mechanical work: templates, CSS, boilerplate CRUD.

### 29.2. Full documentation in context — always
The coder receives ALL documentation parts in every session: full ai_plan, ui_plan, DEV_Plan, human_plan, agents_rule. Partial context is forbidden — tested empirically (April 2026, DeepSeek 3.2 / Qwen 3.6): without the full picture the coder hallucinates missing details instead of asking. Full documentation fits comfortably in the 1M context window.

Counter-measure for long-context degradation: the critical sections for the current step (FIFO filter matrix §7.1, pinned versions §1.3, the step's own «Разделы» references) are ADDITIONALLY restated or pointed to in the step prompt — so they sit close to the working position, not only far back in context.

### 29.3. Library versions in every coding session
ai_plan §1.3 (pinned library versions) must be present in the context of every coding session. Without it the coder may emit deprecated or too-new syntax.

### 29.4. Critical prohibitions repeated per step
The prohibitions «no ORM (SQLAlchemy Core only)», «Decimal for all money/quantity values», «no enqueue/socket/SMTP inside a transaction» must be restated in the prompt of every step where they apply. A prohibition stated once at session start loses force as context grows.

### 29.5. Session rules for Qwen (frontend coder)
- Qwen executes specifications; it does not make architecture or UX decisions. If ui_plan (ч.1 или ч.2) does not cover a case — STOP and ask (§14 format), do not invent layout or behavior.
- Iterative workflow is the norm: first output is reviewed, corrections are given as a concrete numbered list (specific selectors, values, behaviors — not "make it better"), then one revision pass. Qwen excels at targeted fixes.
- Known drift risks to check after every step: (1) English strings in user-facing templates; (2) returning full pages or JSON where an HTMX fragment is required; (3) pulling in React/Vue patterns instead of the project stack (Bootstrap 5 + HTMX + Alpine.js); (4) creating a separate mobile template instead of media queries inside the same template (тип Д rule); (5) replacing the documented pagination (25/50/100 per page) with infinite scroll via hx-trigger="revealed" — pagination is the requirement, infinite scroll is forbidden.
- Full documentation in context — same as §29.2, applies to Qwen equally.

## 30. vkbot — deterministic command executor (node 7730)

### 30.0. What it is and who this section is for
vkbot is a deterministic command executor with no AI layer of its own, running on node 7730, reachable via Telegram. It executes exactly what is written in a command block — no interpretation, no judgment calls. This section applies to chat-based AI agents working on this project (architect, backend coder, frontend coder) that have NO direct access to the bot or the filesystem — Ilya is the only relay: he copies the AI-formulated command block (or forwards the attached file) into the Telegram chat himself. Exception (27.07.2026): agents running directly on the server with filesystem access (Claude Code) edit project files directly and do not use vkbot command blocks. Whichever agent is producing a file correction or a deployment/ops action must format it using this command syntax, ready to forward as-is, not as prose.

### 30.1. Project folder convention
- D:\projects\sklad-app\ — root: planning/spec documents (ai_plan, human_plan, ui_plan, DEV_Plan, agents_rule, demo_data) plus miscellaneous project material.
- D:\projects\sklad-app\erp-project\ — the actual working application: Flask app, migrations, templates, static files, everything the ERP system is built from.
FILE / PATH / SRC are relative to D:\projects\ unless given as an absolute path. A spec document is sklad-app/ai_plan_part_3.md; an application file is sklad-app/erp-project/app.py or sklad-app/erp-project/services/cost_service.py. Getting the erp-project/ segment wrong is the single most likely path mistake — always include it for application code, never for documentation.

Other paths relevant to specific commands:
- D:\scripts\commands\ and D:\scripts\commands\auto\ — scripts invoked via ACTION: cmd (auto\ runs daily at 08:20, see §30.8).
- D:\staging\ — inbox for files sent to the bot via Telegram; auto-cleared of files older than 7 days.
- D:\Archive\ — created by archive, source for unzip. D:\Archive\_history\ — per-file version history used by rollback.

D:\projects\ also contains other unrelated repositories (Parabern, Open-Claw, various Factorio mod projects, a test repo). They are out of scope for this document — agents working on this ERP project use REPO: erp-project (or sklad-app for the documentation root) and should not reference other repo names.

### 30.2. Command block syntax
ACTION: <command_name>
KEY1: value
KEY2: value (may be multiline)

A key is recognized only at column 0 of a line (KEY:). Its value is everything up to the next such key, including line breaks. One leading space after the colon is stripped; all further indentation is preserved verbatim — critical for code where indentation is significant.

Known parser keys: ACTION, FILE, FIND, REPLACE, CONTENT, REPO, MESSAGE, LINES, PATH, SCRIPT, DEST, BRANCH, METHOD, DIRECTION, SRC, NAME, TIMEOUT, STEPS, FORCE, RANGE.

Fenced regions are skip-zones for key-scanning: lines inside a triple-backtick fence are never scanned for KEY: patterns. This is what makes it SAFE to put a literal vkbot command example inside a FIND/REPLACE/CONTENT value — which is exactly what happens whenever a correction documents or patches vkbot's own syntax (e.g. inside agents_rule.md itself, or any document that explains this command format).
MANDATORY rule for self-referential content: whenever a FIND, REPLACE, or CONTENT value needs to contain example text that itself looks like a command block (lines starting with ACTION:, FILE:, FIND:, etc.), that example MUST be wrapped in a fenced block within the value. Without the fence, the parser will treat the embedded ACTION:/FILE:/etc. lines as real top-level keys, truncating the actual value early and corrupting the patch. This is distinct from — and does not relax — the rule in §30.5 against wrapping an entire outer file in a single pair of fences.

### 30.3. Command reference and when to use each

**patch** — find/replace inside an existing file. Default tool for any documentation correction or small/medium code fix. Replaces the first occurrence of FIND; if FIND is not found the bot reports an explicit error and the file is untouched.
```
ACTION: patch
FILE: sklad-app/erp-project/app.py
FIND: def old_func(
REPLACE: def new_func(
```

**create** — new file with inline CONTENT. Only for short files (roughly under ~30 lines); anything longer — use write. Keys: FILE, CONTENT.

**write** — replace a file entirely via attachment. For full-file rewrites, new files over ~30 lines, or when more than ~30% of a file changes. Attach the file in Telegram with caption `ACTION: write` + `FILE: <path>`.

**delete** — delete a file or folder. Key: FILE. Irreversible, no confirmation inside the bot. Use it exactly when deletion is the correct action — no extra confirmation ritual is layered on top by agents_rule; the bot's own irreversibility is the only safeguard, by design.

**rollback** — revert a file to a previous saved version. Key: FILE, optional STEPS. Before every overwrite via patch/create/write, the bot silently saves a copy to D:\Archive\_history\ (last 5 versions kept per file). No STEPS → the version right before the last edit; STEPS: 2 → two versions back. Deliberately simple — always "the last saved one", no version picking. Use instead of crafting a manual reverse patch.

**mkdir** — create a folder. Key: PATH.

**git** — commit + push. Keys: REPO, MESSAGE, optional BRANCH. Use after Ilya confirms a change is good — typically after a DEV_Plan step is accepted or a documentation batch is applied. "Nothing to commit" is not an error.

**pull** — fetch changes made directly via the GitHub web UI. Key: REPO. Use before resuming local/bot work if a change might have been made outside the normal patch/write flow.

**log** — tail of a log or any text file. Keys: REPO (short name: watchdog, tunnel, xray, xray-watchdog, vkbot — or a direct path to any text file), LINES. Use for diagnosing a misbehaving service before deciding on a fix.

**status** — status of all node services. No keys. First diagnostic step before log, when something seems down.

**dir** — list files and folders, top-level only, folders separated from files, sizes in KB. Key: PATH. Use to inspect a directory before deciding what to patch or where to write.

**extract** — pull a line range from a file into a downloadable attachment instead of inline text. Keys: FILE, RANGE (e.g. 100-200). For large or special-character-heavy excerpts where inline text would risk Telegram's message-length or Markdown limits.

**archive** — pack a folder into a zip. Keys: PATH, DEST. Use before sync (folders cannot be synced directly) and as a manual backup before risky operations (e.g. destructive migration), in addition to the automatic daily backup (§30.8).

**unzip** — smart-extract a zip, handling the common single-wrapping-folder case. Keys: FILE, DEST. Restores from an archive backup or unpacks a zip uploaded via sync.

**build** — run the project's build script. Keys: REPO, SCRIPT (must already exist in the repo). Use after a code change that requires a build step (frontend bundling etc.).

**sync** — upload/download a single file to/from FTP or WebDAV (mail.ru cloud). Keys: METHOD (ftp/webdav), DIRECTION (upload/download), SRC, DEST. Files only — folders are intentionally not supported (recursive sync risks pushing .git/.env/service files to external storage). For a folder: archive → sync the zip → unzip on the other end.

**cmd** — run a custom one-off script. Keys: NAME, optional TIMEOUT. Scripts live in D:\scripts\commands\ (.ps1 or .py), with commands\auto\ as the daily auto-run set (§30.8). For ad-hoc diagnostics or utilities that don't fit any built-in action. Runs asynchronously — does not block other bot commands, unlike everything else. The script writes its own result to <name>.log next to itself; once the process exits, the bot reads that file and sends it. Default timeout 600s; on timeout the bot finds the process by the script's full path and force-kills it. A script can also be attached directly (caption ACTION: cmd, optional NAME:/TIMEOUT:) — the bot saves it into D:\scripts\commands\ and runs it immediately; if a file with that name exists, the bot refuses to overwrite silently — it lists existing files and requires FORCE: yes.

**batch** — multiple actions in one file. The default delivery format for anything non-trivial — see §30.4.

### 30.4. Batch format and the separator
Blocks are separated by a line containing five or more = characters and nothing else, on its own line. This is the ONLY block boundary the parser recognizes — never use a line of ===== inside a FIND/REPLACE/CONTENT value, and never put any other text on the separator line.
Example:
```
ACTION: patch
FILE: sklad-app/ai_plan_part_3.md
FIND: ...
REPLACE: ...
=====
ACTION: patch
FILE: sklad-app/human_plan_part_2.md
FIND: ...
REPLACE: ...
```
A batch is sent as a .txt file attachment with caption ACTION: batch. Plain text without an attachment makes the bot wait for the file on the next message.

### 30.5. Delivery channel rule (applies to every AI agent producing a command block for Ilya)
Telegram's chat editor can mangle structure on copy-paste: markdown-sensitive characters (asterisk, underscore, backtick), multi-line indentation, trailing whitespace are all at risk of corruption when typed or pasted directly into a chat message.
- Inline chat text is allowed ONLY for a single, single-line FIND/REPLACE pair with no markdown-sensitive characters and no indentation to preserve.
- Everything else — multi-line FIND/REPLACE/CONTENT, more than one correction, any text containing asterisk, underscore, backticks, or significant indentation — is delivered as a .txt file, even for a single action, for consistency.
- The OUTER file itself is never wrapped in a single pair of triple-backtick fences (that would just add literal fence characters to the first/last value). Fences are used ONLY around individual embedded examples inside a value, per the mandatory rule in §30.2, when the content being patched is itself about vkbot's command syntax.

### 30.6. Typical sequences

Mandatory order for any change delivery to the project: **archive → patch/batch → git**. The order is never reversed or shortened, except in cases explicitly agreed with Ilya.

- Documentation correction: archive → patch/batch → git commit once Ilya confirms the change set is final.
- Code change: archive → patch or write → build (if the change needs it) → status/log to confirm the service is healthy → git commit + push.
- A fix regressed something: rollback the affected file(s) rather than hand-crafting a reverse patch, then reassess.
- Diagnosing a problem: status → log → decide the fix → patch → build (if needed) → status again to confirm.
- Backup before a risky operation: archive → sync upload (ftp/webdav). Note the daily full-repo backup (§30.8) already provides a baseline safety net; this manual step is for an immediate, operation-specific snapshot.
- Restore: sync download → unzip.
- Resuming after a manual GitHub edit: pull before any further patch/write to that repo.

### 30.7. Error handling and safety net (informational — affects what to expect, not how to write commands)
Any exception during execution is caught and returned as "Ошибка выполнения: <reason>" — failures are always explicit, never silent. If output text breaks Telegram's Markdown parser, the bot automatically retries without Markdown formatting. Every command is logged to C:\logs\vkbot.log.
Before writing any .py or .json file (patch, create, write, or cmd's script attachment), the bot validates syntax first (ast.parse for Python, json.loads for JSON) — an invalid result is rejected with the exact line/error and the file is left untouched. This is a safety net, not a substitute for writing correct code.

### 30.8. Automated backups and scheduled tasks (context only — not actions agents issue)
A daily full backup of D:\projects (every repo) runs at 08:00: encrypted 7z (AES-256 + header encryption) uploaded to WebDAV, 10-version rotation kept both locally (D:\Archive\) and remotely. Watchdog kills the backup process if it hangs over 20 minutes; if no fresh backup marker exists by 08:30, an error is logged.
Not covered by this backup: Xray configs, .env files, the bot itself — out of scope for this project's agents.
Other scheduled tasks: 07:00 git pull across all repos; 08:15 a health digest (disk/RAM/Docker/VPN/git status/yesterday's backup status); 08:20 runs every script in commands\auto\ (same mechanism as cmd).
A watchdog process checks every 2 minutes that the tunnel, xray-watchdog, and vkbot itself are alive, including an actual heartbeat check for vkbot (not just process presence) — restarts it if unresponsive.
Practical implication: the daily backup and per-file rollback (§30.3) together mean most operations no longer need a manual archive step purely for safety — reserve manual archive+sync for the moment right before something specifically destructive.

This supersedes the earlier "Файл: ... / НАЙТИ: ... / ЗАМЕНИТЬ НА: ..." prose format for all project-file corrections and ops actions going forward.

### 30.9. Default assumption: applied unless reported otherwise

If Ilya has not reported that a patch/batch/correction was not applied, or reported a problem applying it, assume by default that it was applied successfully. The process is fully automated through vkbot and takes seconds, so a separate "applied" confirmation is not required for every correction. If application failed or was skipped, Ilya states this explicitly, and the assumed state is revised.

---

## 31. Subagents and context economy (added 30.07.2026)

### 31.1. Default: delegate whenever delegation is possible

If the environment provides subagents, the main agent delegates by default. Every tool call the main agent makes itself — file listings, greps, command output, test logs — stays in its context forever and pushes the session toward a summarisation cutoff. A subagent burns its own context and returns only the conclusion.

Rule: before doing something yourself, ask «could a subagent do this and hand me back three lines?» If yes — delegate.

### 31.2. Cheap models for routine work

Routine and mechanical operations go to the cheapest fast model available (Haiku), not to the main model. Routine means: the outcome is verifiable, the instructions are exact, and the chance of a judgement error is effectively zero.

Delegate to a cheap model:
- git operations: status, add, commit with a given message, push, branch checks
- running tests, lint, migrations; collecting their output
- searching files, counting occurrences, listing structure
- mechanical mass edits with an exact find/replace list
- checking a result against a written checklist

Never delegate (the main agent does these itself):
- architectural decisions and choices between options
- edits to the specification documents (human_plan, ai_plan, ui_plan, DEV_Plan, agents_rule)
- resolving contradictions between documents
- business logic, algorithms, anything requiring project context
- anything where «what exactly to do» is not yet decided

### 31.3. How to write a task for a subagent

- Exact commands or exact edits, step by step. No «figure it out», no «improve if needed».
- State the expected result of each step, so the subagent can detect failure itself.
- Explicit stop condition: on any error — return the exact error text and stop, do not attempt repairs.
- Explicit prohibition: do not commit, do not change files, do not create or delete branches unless the task says so.

### 31.4. Destructive operations are never delegated implicitly

A subagent task must not contain destructive operations that Ilya did not explicitly request by name: deleting branches (local or remote), force-push, rm, dropping database objects, overwriting files outside the stated scope. If such an action seems necessary — the main agent asks Ilya first, then delegates with the exact target named.

### 31.5. Verify state before delegating

Before delegating any git or filesystem operation, the main agent re-checks the current state (branch name, working tree, applied migrations). Ilya merges and pushes on his own; the main agent's memory of «which branch we are on» goes stale between turns, and a subagent will faithfully execute an outdated instruction.

### 31.6. Reporting

The subagent's report is not shown to Ilya. The main agent extracts what matters and states it in Russian in its own answer, including failures. Never present a delegated result as more certain than the subagent's own wording; never invent a result for a subagent that has not finished.

---

## FINAL RULE
If there is a choice:
ASK FIRST → THEN DO
Never the opposite.

## 1. ТЕХНИЧЕСКИЙ СТЕК

| Компонент | Решение |
| --- | --- |
| Бэкенд | Flask (Python) |
| База данных | PostgreSQL >= 15 (требование обусловлено использованием NULLS NOT DISTINCT в уникальных индексах) |
| Работа с БД | SQLAlchemy Core (Table, MetaData, select/insert/update). ORM — только для чтения в сложных отчётах (гибридный подход) |
| Фронтенд | Bootstrap 5 + HTMX + Alpine.js. Все библиотеки — локальные копии в `/static/vendor/`, загрузка с CDN запрещена (система работает без интернета, см. human_plan §1 и ui_plan ч.1 §1) |
| Шаблонизатор | Jinja2 |
| Развёртывание | Docker Compose (сервисы: flask, postgres, redis, rq-worker, nginx) |
| Миграции | Alembic. Миграции пишутся вручную (SQLAlchemy Core не поддерживает autogenerate). Каждое изменение структуры БД — отдельный файл миграции написанный разработчиком. Применяются командой `flask db upgrade`. В dev-режиме — автоматически. Миграции — единственный источник истины о структуре БД. Файлы `<модуль>/models/tables.py` с определениями `Table()` НЕ пишутся вручную и НЕ редактируются: они генерируются из применённой схемы собственной командой `flask gen-models` (реализация — core/services/model_generator.py, внешних генераторов не используем) и коммитятся в репозиторий. Раскладка таблиц по модулям (core / purchase / production) задана маппингом внутри генератора. Ручное редактирование сгенерированных файлов запрещено (в шапке каждого — маркер AUTOGENERATED). Порядок работы: (1) написать миграцию, (2) `flask db upgrade`, (3) `flask gen-models`. Тест `tests/test_schema_sync.py` сверяет определения `Table()` с фактической схемой БД (имена таблиц, колонок, типы, nullable) и падает при расхождении — это машинная защита от рассинхрона. |
| | Каждая миграция должна быть идемпотентной: повторный запуск alembic upgrade не должен ломать базу. Использовать IF NOT EXISTS для CREATE, IF EXISTS для DROP. Никогда не менять структуру БД напрямую через SQL-консоль в обход миграций. |
| | Миграции данных: при добавлении NOT NULL колонки в существующую таблицу миграция ОБЯЗАНА в том же файле заполнить значения для существующих строк (UPDATE backfill или server_default), и только затем установить ограничение NOT NULL. Оставлять существующие строки с NULL в обязательном поле — запрещено. При изменении кодировки статусов или ENUM — миграция содержит UPDATE существующих записей на новые значения. |
| | Процедура отката миграции: 1. alembic downgrade -1 — откатить последнюю миграцию. 2. Если данные повреждены — восстановить из резервной копии (§9). 3. Исправить миграцию и применить заново. Перед применением на prod — проверить миграцию на тестовой БД. |
| Фоновые задачи | Redis + Python RQ |
| Хеширование паролей | `werkzeug.security`, алгоритм `pbkdf2:sha256` |
| Сессии | В Redis — через пакет Flask-Session (backend: redis), та же инстанция что и для RQ. Redis запускается с persistence (appendonly yes), иначе его рестарт разлогинит всех. HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax. Таймаут 60 минут с обновлением при активности |
| CSRF | Flask-WTF |
| Excel | openpyxl |
| PDF | WeasyPrint (HTML+CSS → PDF через Jinja2-шаблон). reportlab и любая императивная отрисовка по координатам запрещены — печатные формы верстаются как HTML |
| Импорт данных | pandas |
| Язык интерфейса | Русский. Тексты хардкодятся в шаблонах. Тексты подсказок — `/hints/hints.json` |
| Терминология UI | «Приёмка» — раздел интерфейса (навигация, заголовки страниц). «Оприходование» — название операции/документа (ОП). В коде: класс `GoodsReceipt`. Единственное каноническое имя сервиса приёмки/оприходования — `GoodsReceiptService` (файл purchase/services/goods_receipt_service.py). Имена ReceiptService, PostingService и любые другие варианты запрещены. |
| Мониторинг | Логирование запросов выполняющихся более 1 секунды |

### 1.1. Обязательные стандарты типов данных

Decimal везде — для веса, количества, цен, остатков использовать исключительно `Decimal` из модуля `decimal`. Использование `float` категорически запрещено.

Нормализация ввода — в контроллерах перед парсингом числовых полей заменять `,` на `.`.

Время сотрудников — хранить в минутах (int). Округление вниз: 1 час 20 мин 31 сек → 80 минут. Секунды не хранятся.

### 1.2. Структура hints.json

```json
{
  "purchase_request.delivery_date": "Плановая дата когда ожидается поставка.",
  "stock_batch.expiry_date": "Дата истечения срока годности партии.",
  "route_name.field_name": "Текст подсказки."
}
```

Ключи формата `route_name.field_name`. `route_name` — имя Blueprint маршрута, `field_name` — атрибут `name` поля формы. Шаблоны читают подсказки через хелпер `hint(key)`. Если ключ не найден — иконка «?» не отображается.

## 2.1. ЧАСОВЫЕ ПОЯСА И ВРЕМЯ  

Все временные поля в БД — тип `timestamptz`, хранение всегда в UTC (PostgreSQL делает это автоматически для timestamptz). В Python — только aware datetime (`datetime.now(timezone.utc)`), naive datetime запрещён. Серверные значения времени — через `NOW()` БД, не через время приложения. Отображение в интерфейсе и печатных формах — в часовом поясе из system_settings (ключ `display_timezone`, default: Europe/Moscow). Поля типа `date` (даты документов, сроки годности) — календарные даты без пояса, хранятся как есть.  

## 3. СЛОИ АРХИТЕКТУРЫ

Data Layer: определение таблиц через SQLAlchemy Core (Table, MetaData). Только явные схемы. Связи — через ForeignKey, без relationship (кроме ORM-чтения в отчётах).

Service Layer: вся бизнес-логика. Работа с БД — явные запросы (select, insert, update) с транзакциями и `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` для критических операций. Валидации на уровне Python, вызываются из сервисов.

Flask Layer: маршруты (blueprints), вызов сервисов, рендеринг шаблонов. Без бизнес-логики в маршрутах.

### 3.1. Правило атомарности транзакций

Интеграции (email, Telegram, печать этикеток) запрещено выполнять внутри транзакции БД. Паттерн реализации:

```python
def post_goods_receipt(receipt_id):
    with get_connection() as conn:
        with conn.begin():
            # ... операции с БД ...
            pass  # ← здесь COMMIT
    # ← явный вызов ПОСЛЕ транзакции
    queue.enqueue('send_notification', receipt_id=receipt_id)
```

Любой queue.enqueue(), send_email(), print_label() находится строго после выхода из контекстного менеджера транзакции.

Проверяется через чеклист §25.11 и правило LINT-005.

**Обработка ошибок при проведении документов:**

При любой ошибке внутри транзакции проведения:
- Транзакция откатывается автоматически (PostgreSQL) или явно через rollback()
- Flask exception handler логирует ошибку в error.log с stack trace
- HTMX получает HTTP 400 с текстом ошибки на русском
- Toast-уведомление показывает текст ошибки пользователю
- Документ остаётся в статусе draft
- audit_log записывает неудачную попытку: action='post_failed', details={error: 'описание'}
- Автоматического retry нет — пользователь нажимает «Провести» снова

Формат ошибки для HTMX: HTTP 400, body: «Не удалось провести документ: {причина на русском}». Технические детали (stack trace) — только в error.log, не пользователю.

Пример реализации (app.py). Стандартные HTTP-ошибки (403, 404, 405 и т.д.) пропускаются без изменений — иначе они превратятся в 400 и нарушат конвенцию ответов ниже. Отката БД в обработчике нет: соединения контекстно-управляемые (SQLAlchemy Core), транзакция откатывается при выходе из блока with:

```python
from werkzeug.exceptions import HTTPException

@app.errorhandler(Exception)
def handle_posting_error(e):
    if isinstance(e, HTTPException):
        return e
    app.logger.error(f"Posting error: {e}", exc_info=True)
    if request.headers.get('HX-Request'):
        return str(e), 400
    return render_template('error.html', error=str(e)), 400
```

**Health check endpoint:**

Маршрут /healthcheck доступен без авторизации.
Используется Docker HEALTHCHECK и мониторингом.
Проверяет:
- Доступность PostgreSQL: SELECT 1
- Доступность Redis: ping()

Ответ при успехе (HTTP 200): `{"db": true, "redis": true, "status": "ok"}`
Ответ при проблеме (HTTP 503): `{"db": false, "redis": true, "status": "degraded"}`

Маршрут не логируется в audit_log и не требует CSRF-токена. Исключение из CSRF через @csrf.exempt декоратор.

**Параметры SQLAlchemy connection pool:**

Engine создаётся ОДИН РАЗ при старте приложения (модуль core/database.py). Все сервисы используют один и тот же engine через get_connection().

```python
create_engine(
    DATABASE_URL,
    pool_size=5,        # 5 постоянных соединения
    max_overflow=10,    # +10 при пиковой нагрузке (итого макс 15)
    pool_timeout=30,    # ждать свободное соединение 30 сек
    pool_recycle=3600,  # пересоздавать соединение каждый час
    pool_pre_ping=True, # проверять соединение перед использованием
)
```

Обоснование: 10 пользователей × HTMX (несколько запросов на страницу) × возможные долгие FIFO-запросы. Pool exhaustion → HTTP 500. pool_pre_ping=True обязателен — PostgreSQL закрывает idle соединения.

**CSRF protection:**

Все POST/PUT/DELETE маршруты защищены CSRF-токеном. Реализация через Flask-WTF CSRFProtect.

```python
from flask_wtf.csrf import CSRFProtect
csrf = CSRFProtect(app)
```

HTMX автоматически передаёт токен если добавить в base.html:
```html
<meta name="csrf-token" content="{{ csrf_token() }}">
```

И настроить HTMX:
```javascript
document.body.addEventListener('htmx:configRequest', (e) => {
    e.detail.headers['X-CSRFToken'] =
        document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]').content;
});
```

Исключения из CSRF: /healthcheck. Исключения настраиваются через @csrf.exempt декоратор.

**Конвенция ответов для HTMX маршрутов:**

- Успешная операция возвращающая HTML-фрагмент: → HTTP 200, render_template('_partial.html', ...)
- Успешная операция без контента (удаление, действие): → HTTP 200, пустой body или toast-сообщение
- Ошибка валидации (неверные данные): → HTTP 400, текст ошибки на русском → HTMX показывает через hx-target или toast
- Ошибка авторизации: → HTTP 403, текст «Недостаточно прав»
- Серверная ошибка: → HTTP 500, «Внутренняя ошибка сервера. Обратитесь к администратору.» → Детали только в error.log
- Редирект после успешной операции: → HTTP 200 с заголовком HX-Redirect: /url → Не использовать HTTP 302 для HTMX-запросов
- JSON ответы (только для Alpine.js или JavaScript): → HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/json → Использовать только если HTML-фрагмент невозможен
- Toast через HX-Trigger (предпочтительный способ): → HTTP 200 с заголовком: `HX-Trigger: {"showToast": {"message": "Документ проведён", "type": "success"}}` → Alpine.js или JavaScript слушает событие showToast и показывает уведомление → Использовать вместо возврата HTML-фрагмента toast когда основной контент уже обновлён

Сессии хранятся в Redis (Flask-Session, backend redis). Переживают перезапуск контейнера приложения и масштабируются на несколько воркеров без изменений кода.

/healthcheck — публичный endpoint без авторизации и CSRF. Возвращает только статус инфраструктуры (DB, Redis). Не содержит бизнес-данных.

## 4. ЛОГИРОВАНИЕ

Файловые логи с ротацией (до 10 файлов по 10 МБ):
- `app.log` — уровень INFO. Включает запросы >1 секунды.
- `error.log` — уровень ERROR. Полный стек-трейс.
- `audit.log` — действия пользователей (дублируется в таблицу `audit_log`).

Администратор может включить уровень DEBUG через `system_settings`. Оператор видит человеко-читаемое сообщение с кодом ошибки (например: «Недостаточно свободного остатка (ERR-1234)»). Стек-трейс — только в `error.log`.

Обязательный формат логирования в сервисах:
```python
logger.info(f"🟡 START {function_name}: {key_params}")
logger.info(f"✅ SUCCESS {function_name}: {result_summary}")
logger.error(f"❌ FAIL {function_name}: error={str(e)}")
```

END ai_plan_part_1.md

## 16. ПЕРВЫЙ ЗАПУСК

Из `.env`: `ADMIN_LOGIN`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`.

При первом запуске (нет ни одного пользователя):
- Сотрудник «Администратор» (запись в employees) + пользователь-администратор (role=admin), связанный с ним через employee_id — связь обязательна (§5.1)
- Единицы: шт (0), кг (3), м (3)
- Иерархия мест хранения: «Основное здание» (level=building) → «Основной склад» (level=room). Иерархия намеренно неполная — администратор сам создаёт нужные уровни ниже (стеллажи, ячейки).
- Группы номенклатуры: «Общая» (без флагов), «Полуфабрикаты» (is_semi_finished = true), «Готовые устройства» (is_finished_goods = true), «Готовая продукция» (is_finished_goods = true)
- Валюты: Рубль (RUB), Доллар (USD)
- Записи в `document_numbering` для всех типов документов
- Аналитические категории (6 штук, создаются в init_service): Комплектующие, Печатные платы, Корпусные изделия, Монтаж, Сопутствующие товары, Услуги.
- Установить system_settings: commissioning_mode = false, default_vat_rate = 20, oui_prefix = '00:21:1A', work_day_start = '10:00', work_day_end = '19:00'

Остальные ключи system_settings (SMTP, telegram_bot_token, backup_schedule, archive_period_years, debug_mode, display_timezone, stale_task_days, company_*, order_status_colors, sn_external_prefix) при первом запуске НЕ создаются: сервис настроек при первом обращении к отсутствующему ключу возвращает значение по умолчанию из §5.5 и создаёт запись. Это позволяет добавлять новые ключи без миграций данных.

Демо-номенклатура, контрагенты, техкарты и маршрутные карты не создаются. Запрещено.

telegram_bot_token — не обязателен при первом запуске. NULL допустим, уведомления не работают до привязки токена.

Цвета статусов заказов (order_status_colors): `{"draft": "#F5F5F5", "posted": "#43A047", "cancelled": "#E53935", "closed": "#616161"}`

Таблицы: все из §5.1 (nomenclature_groups, units_of_measure, nomenclature, nomenclature_versions, nomenclature_modifications, nomenclature_substitutes, storage_locations, contractors, employees, users, currencies, currency_rates, label_printers, user_location_permissions, document_numbering, system_settings, user_settings, audit_log)

Результат: работающий интерфейс со справочниками и авторизацией.

**Этап 1б — FIFO движки + тесты**

Таблицы: stock_batches, stock_balances, stock_movements, stock_transfers, stock_transfer_items, write_offs, write_off_items, min_stock_alerts, goods_receipts, goods_receipt_items (для оприходования без поставщика; FK stock_batches.receipt_item_id добавляется на Этапе 2).

Функциональность: складской учёт (FIFO с версиями, резервирование, движения, перемещения, списание, оприходование).

Миграция индексов FIFO (выполняется в конце Этапа 1б, до перехода к Этапу 1в):
```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_stock_batches_fifo
  ON stock_batches (nomenclature_id, version_id, location_id, batch_date, id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_stock_balances_unique
  ON stock_balances (nomenclature_id, version_id, location_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_stock_movements_document
  ON stock_movements (document_type, document_id);
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_stock_movements_created
  ON stock_movements (created_at);
```
Остальные индексы из §20 создаются на Этапе 4 (Шаг 25).

Результат: полностью рабочий складской учёт с тестами и корректными FIFO-индексами.

**Этап 1в — Аудит + полировка**

Функциональность: audit_log, min_stock_alerts, пересчёт остатков, глобальная заморозка.

Полное покрытие тестами обязательно перед переходом к Этапу 2.


## 21. ОГРАНИЧЕНИЯ, ЗАФИКСИРОВАННЫЕ ЯВНО

- Иерархия групп номенклатуры — только 1 уровень.
- Версии номенклатуры несовместимы между собой — замена версий запрещена.
- Замены — только между разными номенклатурами, направление важно (несимметрично).
- Остатки ведутся на уровне версии, не аналога.
- Аналоги (nomenclature_modifications) — справочная информация, фиксируется в партии при приёмке.
- Конвертация единиц измерения — не предусмотрена.
- Учёт праздников и выходных — не ведётся.
- Внешние API и 1С — отсутствуют.
- Горизонтальное масштабирование — не требуется.
- Бэкап `/uploads` — вне рамок ТЗ.
- НДС при возврате — не пересчитывается.
- Удаление записей при наличии любых ссылок (движения, документы, техкарты) — запрещено для всех ролей включая администратора; вывод из оборота — деактивация (is_active = false). Записи без единой ссылки удаляются физически (§7.19, ADR-007). Мягкого удаления и восстановления в системе нет.
- Кеширование справочников — не реализуется на Этапах 1–4. Все запросы к справочникам выполняются напрямую через сервисные методы (`NomenclatureService`, `LocationService` и т.д.). Прямые `SELECT` в маршрутах Flask или шаблонах Jinja2 запрещены. Триггер для введения Redis-кеша: среднее время запросов к справочникам >200 мс при нагрузке 30+ пользователей по данным `app.log`.
- Все обращения к `stock_movements` выполняются только через `MovementService.get_movements(...)`. Прямые SELECT в маршрутах и шаблонах запрещены.
- История движений в отчётах: если запрошенный период полностью в текущих данных — запрос только к `stock_movements`. Если период захватывает архив — `UNION ALL` с `archive_movements`. `stock_balances` и себестоимость считаются только по текущим данным, архив не участвует.
- Задание = одна операция маршрутной карты.
- Резервирование только при переводе задания в `in_work`.
- `float` запрещён — только `Decimal`.
- Бизнес-логика в Flask Layer запрещена.
- Интеграции внутри транзакции запрещены — только через RQ после коммита.
- НИОКР-партии исключаются из расчёта себестоимости готовой продукции.
- Ручной пересчёт `stock_balances` — доступен администратору через кнопку «Пересчитать остатки» в глобальных настройках. Выполняется без создания документов. Флаг `global_freeze` в `system_settings` устанавливается временно на время пересчёта и снимается автоматически после завершения. При старте приложения флаг сбрасывается в false автоматически.
- Добавление дочернего узла в место хранения где есть партии товара — запрещено. Сервис проверяет наличие партий в `stock_batches` по `location_id` перед созданием дочернего узла. Если партии есть — операция отклоняется с сообщением: «Невозможно создать вложенный уровень: в "[название места]" есть товар. Переместите товар вручную и повторите.»
- Понятные пояснения при отсутствии обязательных справочных данных: если система обнаруживает что не хватает обязательного элемента (группы номенклатуры, единицы измерения, валюты, места хранения) — действие блокируется с сообщением на русском языке без технических деталей. Формат: «Невозможно выполнить действие: не найдена [название элемента]. Обратитесь к администратору.» Стек-трейс показывается только в `error.log`.

End ai_plan_part_10.md
